newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Singapore trader eyes jet fuel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Singapore trader eyes jet fuel.

text.p: A Singapore trader who has bought about 14 million of gas oil, is now eyeing jet fuel as well, buying 600,000 barrels this week, traders said.
But they noted that despite the trader's buying spree, jet prices have actually dipped from levels earlier this week.

The trader on Thursday bought two 100,000-barrel cargoes from the same seller, a European major at $24.90 per barrel for May 2-6 lifting free-on-board (fob) and $25.30 for May 13-17. The deals were 10 cents and 30 cents per barrel lower from Wednesday's sales, respectively .
Traders noted that the jet fuel market is in contango as regional demand for prompt cargoes are soft while they expect demand to pick up in later months.
Another European major sold 150,000 barrels of gas oil to a Japanese trader at $26.95 per barrel for May 13-17 lifting fob.
The major that sold the jet cargoes was also offering a gas oil cargo to a Singapore trader at $27.60 for early May lifting, but no deals were concluded.
Traders also said that Indonesia has bought 80,000 tonnes of gas oil from a Western trader at 10 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, for first-half May delivery, cost-and-freight basis.
Gas oil swaps rose with May being last quoted at $25.75/$25.85, 15 cents more than Wednesday.
